title: British Museum: Roman Republican freed couple, 1867,0508.55

title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Class System iii

title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Class System iv

title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Dehqan
scope: Landed dehqan identity and its changing meaning over time.

title: Metropolitan Museum: The Art of the Mamluk Period
scope: Mamluk military institution, Turkic and Circassian recruitment, acquired Arabic instruction.

title: Metropolitan Museum: The Greater Ottoman Empire, 1600-1800
scope: Imperial institutions, urban commerce and continuing local/ethnic cultural life.

title: Wilanow Palace Museum: Sarmatism
scope: Polish-Lithuanian noble cultural formation; claimed Sarmatian descent is ideology, not an ethnicity assignment.

title: Wilanow Palace Museum: Sarmatism and European culture
scope: Noble political ideals and cultural borrowing; use of the modern scholarly label must be explained.

title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Early New Persian
scope: Middle/New Persian distinction; continued variation, learned use and multiple writing traditions.

title: Len Scales, The Shaping of German Identity: publisher description
scope: Supports a late-medieval broad German identity; not evidence for a single precise ethnogenesis date.

title: Oxford: Lexicon of Greek Personal Names
scope: Ancient naming evidence and regional coverage; use for individual checks, not automatic modern-Greek back-projection.

title: Oxford: LGPN Egypt
scope: Greek/Egyptian personal names with individual provenance and dating.

title: Merchant Adventurers Hall, York: institutional history
scope: Merchant guild and civic institutional setting; not proof that all merchants knew Latin.

title: University course resource: English language timeline

title: Unicode: block ranges

title: Rebecca Lucas: Some names from 15-17th century Latvia
scope: Dated forms in German-language records, distinguished from modern Latvian headings; a small feminine inventory is not proof that the culture is poorly documented.

title: Liviu Marius Ilie: Nunnery Life in 16th Century Wallachia
scope: Musa/Magdalina illustrates a change of name on entering monastic life; abstract and references consulted, not the full paper.

title: Trismegistos: People and Names

title: Romanian Names from the Basarab Line

title: Gooskens et al. (2018), Mutual intelligibility between closely related languages in Europe
scope: Primary research on spoken comprehension, exposure and asymmetry in modern European languages. Supports methodological caution, not any historical engine score.

title: Gooskens and Swarte (2017), Linguistic and extra-linguistic predictors of mutual intelligibility between Germanic languages
scope: Primary research separates exposure and linguistic distance, spoken and written tests. Historical scores in this packet remain authored approximations.

title: Golubovic and Gooskens (2015), Mutual intelligibility between West and South Slavic languages
scope: Primary research concerns modern West/South Slavic test languages, not an empirical reconstruction of medieval Slavic comprehension or Russian-Ukrainian engine scores.

title: Finnish names in historical records — Lea Viljanen
scope: Individual dated forms transcribed from Finnish medieval/early modern records, including Latin and Swedish documentary spellings. Not a census of ethnic Finns.

title: Kaunas names, 1522–1591 — Rebecca Lucas after Alma Ragauskaite
scope: Multilingual town records. Keep recorded nominative spellings and distinguish reconstructed nominatives.

title: Women in Grand Duchy of Lithuania registers — after Jurate Cirunaite
scope: Registers of 1528, 1565, 1567 and 1631; Christian and Muslim repertoires distinguished. Political geography is not proof of Lithuanian vernacular ethnicity.

title: Estonian names from trade and tax records — after Juri Kivimae
scope: Documentary spellings, chiefly sixteenth century; mixed Finnic and Low German recording traditions.

title: Estonian naming patterns — Aryanhwy merch Catmael
scope: Local records, particles and byname examples; editorially reconstructed examples are not individual attestations.

title: Ernst Lewy, Die altpreussischen Personennamen (1904)
scope: Public-domain personal-name corpus. Selected forms from sections 63–67; individual documentary dates not independently extracted.

title: Ivoska, Social Status and Identification of Prussian Women (2023)
scope: Abstract inspected; full article could not be retrieved. It supplies NO name entries in this handoff.

title: Romanian names — Sara L. Uckelman
scope: Dated ruler-name compilation; explicitly elite-biased, not a representative commoner frequency list.

title: Names from the family of Basarab — Jennifer Edwards
scope: Dynastic family-name compilation; dates and vernacular normalisations are not manuscript diplomatic transcriptions.

title: Neagoe Basarab and his family — National History Museum portrait catalogue
scope: Museum identification of sixteenth-century family portrait; Milita, Anghelina, Ruxandra and Stanca. Milita is a Serbian-origin court member.

title: Three Hierarchs monastery foundation inscription
scope: Published inscription text naming Tudosca, Maria and Rucsandra, 1639.

title: Domnita Balasa church
scope: Institutional history of Balasa (1693–1752), foundation of 1743–44; no nineteenth-century donors imported.

title: Matei Basarab and Elina — National History Museum
scope: Museum portrait identification: Elina (c.1598–1653), seventeenth-century fresco.

title: Coptic Church Synaxarion — annual calendar
scope: Names in the Coptic commemorative tradition. This is evidence for devotional repertoire, not birth frequencies, ethnic origin or a dated vernacular manuscript spelling.
kind: primary evidence of a living liturgical tradition

title: Syriaca.org — Syriac Reference Portal
scope: Individual records identify Syriac literary/hagiographic names and primary editions. Saint floruit is NOT the date of the surviving text or the name spelling.

title: Trismegistos Names — public metadata
scope: Specific publicly indexed name records only. No restricted dataset was downloaded. Egyptian documentary location/language does not alone prove religion or ethnicity.

title: Marana and Cyra — Monastic Matrix
scope: Theodoret-related record of two women ascetics; literary personal names, not population frequencies.
kind: research database drawing on primary hagiography

title: Eugenio Lujan — Language and writing among the Lusitanians
scope: Author chapter abstract: Lusitanian inscriptions, Latin alphabet and distinct language treatment. No phonetic reconstruction or intelligibility rate taken from the abstract.

title: Antanas Pakerys, Dvikamienių lietuvių moterų vardų kirčiavimas
kind: linguistic study published by State Commission of the Lithuanian Language
scope: Supports parallel/analogical reconstruction of Lithuanian feminine names. Cross-Baltic use for Prussian fiction is an editorial analogy, not direct Prussian evidence.

title: Vardai VLKK, Moterų vardų kirčiavimo kraipymai
scope: Native compound-name layer and male/female parallel forms; distinguishes historical names from later revival. Does not attest the supplied list of reconstructed female bearers.
